Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses an affinity purification (immunoprecipitation) strategy to capture immune complexes (ICx) using Protein A/G beads and C1q plates. While phosphorylation was set as a variable modification in the search parameters, the primary goal was the identification of immunoglobulin-binding proteins via AP-MS.

scope: Protein A/G magnetic beads or C1q-coated plates were used to capture ICx in the serum of LN, followed by the identification of immunoglobulin-binding proteins using liquid chromatography and tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
The immune complex bound beads were then washed three times with 50 µl PBS.
The washed beads were suspended in 50 µl of 0.1 mg/ml papain solution (0.04 M EDTA, 0.04 M L-cysteine) and incubated at 37°C for 1 h.

100 µl of 200 µg/ml native human C1q was diluted into PBS, coated onto a 96-well microplate (Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA), and incubated overnight at room temperature. ... 100 µl of 1:100 PBS-diluted pooled serum samples was added into the wells and incubated for 2 h at room temperature.
